tagline.text: A 13-tier waterfall on a sacred Mansaka site in the Maragusan Valley, with cool plunge pools

location.label: Location
location.text: Brgy. Coronobe, Maragusan, Davao de Oro

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱600~1,500 (including round-trip transport from Davao, per day)

children.text: Tagbibinta Falls is a multi-tiered waterfall in Barangay Coronobe in the Maragusan Valley of Davao de Oro. Its 13 cascades are considered sacred by the indigenous Mansaka people of Maragusan, and the first tier is an easy walk, making it a refreshing place to swim.
Tagbibinta Falls lies at the foot of Mount Candalaga in Barangay Coronobe, about
6.4 km

from the Maragusan town proper in Davao de Oro (formerly Compostela Valley). Maragusan sits in a highland valley between roughly 600 and 1,500 m above sea level and is nicknamed the "summer capital of the Davao Region" for its cool weather, so many travelers climb up from Davao City for a day or two to escape the heat. The falls are among the easiest of the valley's main attractions to reach.

Travel blogs say the falls have 13 cascades, the last of which plunges about 70 feet (about 21 m) to its base. Locals are said to visit 7 of the tiers, but a blogger who came in 2019 wrote that only the first tier was open and the paths to the others were under construction. A 2022 review reached the falls easily by concrete stairs and paths and saw a waterfall about 50 feet high. The number of tiers and the height differ by source, so check locally which sections are open.

The place is known as sacred to the Mansaka indigenous community of Maragusan, and visitors are asked to keep quiet. It was damaged by Typhoon Pablo in 2012, and the local government and operators have kept developing it; it now works as a mountain resort with rental cottages, restrooms and picnic areas. Thanks to the ice-cold stream water, local families like to come on hot days.

You can visit all year, but Maragusan is a highland area with high annual rainfall, so arriving early, seeing the falls in the morning and moving on to the town or other sights in the afternoon makes it easier to cope with weather changes. The entrance fee was reported as ₱20 in 2019 and ₱30 for adults in 2022, which is very cheap, and the cost stays low even with transport from town. That said, some say development has taken away part of the natural feel. Think of it as a falls where you stroll lightly and dip your feet, not one for rugged trekking. Combined with other waterfalls, hot springs and highland resorts in Maragusan on the same trip it makes a full day, and because the distance makes travel a large part of the trip, I recommend staying one night.

The falls are said to have 13 cascades, with the lowest dropping about 70 feet (about 21 m). Several tiers spill into clear pools, giving the place a calm, peaceful feel. The open sections vary over time, so check locally.
The first tier is described as being "a walk in the park" and is easy to reach. Concrete steps and paths make it manageable for children and older visitors. Watch your step on slippery rocks.
The water is very cold and popular on hot days. Some accounts describe a strong current and hazardous rocks around the pools, so stay in shallow areas and keep an eye on children.
This waterfall is a sacred place for the indigenous Mansaka people of Maragusan. Be respectful by keeping your voice down, leaving no trash and exploring quietly.

Near the falls you will find rental cottages, picnic spots and clean restrooms. It is a good place to rest with a packed lunch and drinks, and one visitor mentioned a swimming pool under construction, so facilities may change.

and nighttime lows about
, much cooler than Davao City. The falls' water is cold and mornings and evenings can feel chilly, so bring a light jacket.

Nearby are Pyalitan Falls, a waterfall with a drop of about 46 m, as well as Kanlawig Hot Spring Resort, Lusaran Mountain Garden Resort and Ayuste Highland Mountain Resort. Pick just one or two a day and take it easy.

items.subtitle: An early start for the falls and the town

children.text: Take a bus or van bound for Maragusan from the Ecoland Terminal or a mall terminal in Davao. The trip takes about
4~5 hours
, so leave early.
Arrive in Maragusan town proper (Poblacion), grab a quick bite and get some small change ready.

Pay the entrance fee and walk to the first tier to swim. Visit only the open sections and follow the signs.
Have lunch and rest at a cottage. If it rains, shorten your plans.
Head back to town and check the last bus time to Davao.
A round trip to Davao in one day is tight, so confirm the last bus time in advance, and if you have time, I recommend the overnight itinerary below.
Leave Davao by bus or van and head up to Maragusan.
Have lunch at a restaurant in town and leave your bags at your lodging.
Spend the afternoon at Tagbibinta Falls.
Return to town to rest at your lodging and have dinner. Reviews mention Maragusan Grill, known for barbecue, and an affordable rice-meal eatery.
The next morning, visit one of Pyalitan Falls, Kanlawig Hot Spring or a highland resort.
After lunch, head back to Davao.
The trail to Pyalitan Falls takes about
15~20 minutes
on foot, but it includes a rock-climbing section, so I recommend a local guide.
There are direct flights from Manila to Davao International Airport (DVO). Airlines and schedules change often, so check the latest timetable before booking.
From Davao airport you can take a taxi, Grab or an airport shuttle into the city. To catch a bus to Maragusan, go to the Ecoland Terminal.
Getting from Manila to Maragusan takes a full day, so it is safer to spend a night in Davao and leave early in the morning.

items.title: From Maragusan town to the falls

children.text: The falls are about
6.4 km
from town, reached by tricycle or habal-habal. In a 2022 review, a one-way tricycle fare was about
Return rides can be scarce, so it is safer to ask the driver in advance to wait or to pick you up.
You can reach Maragusan from Davao by rental car or a car with a driver. The road climbs into a highland valley, so allow plenty of time and drive carefully.
Maragusan is a highland area and stays cool all year. Daytime highs average about
and nights about
, and annual rainfall is high at about 2,261 mm. Rain is said to be heaviest from May to July, so swim less when the falls are swollen.
Mountain weather changes quickly, so showers can come even outside the rainy season. The falls rise fast when it rains and paths get slippery, so check the forecast before you go.

Maragusan town has lodging and restaurants. A 2025 SunStar article stayed at Meadows Maragusan Hotel and Ayuste Highland Mountain Resort, and described Maragusan Grill, known for barbecue, and Dolly's Kitchen House Cafe & Resto, which serves affordable rice and chicken meals. Facilities and operations can change, so check before booking.

There may be no big shops around the falls, so bring water and snacks. If you want to cook your own meal at a cottage, you often need to prepare ingredients beforehand. Maragusan also has Grape Valley, known for its grape farm, and Ancla Farm, which visitors have written about, so you can look around if your schedule allows.
Leave Davao early and spend at least half a day in Maragusan. If you want to make a round trip in one day, be sure to check the last bus time.
Before your visit, it helps to ask the Davao de Oro provincial tourism office or the Maragusan tourism office which sections are open.
Bring swimwear, sandals that can get wet, a towel and a waterproof bag. The stream water is cold.
Bring cash for the entrance fee and cottage rental. In mountain areas, ATMs and card payment are limited.
It is a sacred place for the indigenous Mansaka, so avoid loud noise, drinking and littering.
On rainy days the water rises quickly, so do not enter the water and shorten your plans.
It is convenient to agree on a return time with your tricycle or habal-habal driver in advance.
Bus and van schedules change often. Check the latest notices.
Maragusan is high and cool, so staying long in wet clothes can be cold. Bring dry clothes to change into and a light jacket.
When taking photos, do not climb on the rocks, and keep your phone in a waterproof case.
Accounts describe a strong current and hazardous, slippery rocks. Do not enter the water after rain, when it rises.
The lower falls sections may be closed depending on construction or conditions. Do not cross ropes or signs, and follow local guidance.
The road to Maragusan climbs into the mountains and buses may be infrequent. Do not miss the last ride back.
Signs and fees differ by source. Check the entrance fee and open sections locally.
Keep children close even in shallow water. Assume there is almost no rescue equipment and act accordingly.

Known as a mineral hot spring resort in Poblacion, Maragusan. A good place to relax after the falls.
A resort known for mountain views and its sea of clouds. The mist depends on the weather, so keep your expectations modest.
A very famous waterfall toward Davao Oriental. It is far away, so it is best to treat it as a separate trip.
The starting point and the big city that flights reach. A good place to stay before and after a Maragusan round trip.
